Q1: Sodium nitrite exhibits a comprehensive hazard profile, with several classifications at Tier 1 (Known Hazards) based on the Globally Harmonized System (GHS) for carcinogenicity, mutagenicity, and reproductive effects (CMR), environmental impact (ENV), inhalation (IHL), oral consumption (ORL), and organ/systemic effects (OGN). Additionally, it has Tier 2 (Expanded Perspective) classifications for endocrine disruption (EDC) and dermal/eye hazards (SKN), incorporating more current scientific data beyond GHS conclusions.
Q2: This chemical is identified on key "Lists of Concern," including The Endocrine Disruption Exchange (TEDX list) due to scientific evidence suggesting its potential as an endocrine disruptor. It is also listed under the Clean Water Act, indicating regulatory attention regarding its potential impact on aquatic environments.
Q3: Sodium nitrite is extensively characterized, evidenced by 36,000 scientific literature references, significantly surpassing the median for similar chemicals.
